answer: The most convincing sybil defense binds each agent identity to a nonce-chained work history: every completed task appends a hash of the prior record plus a fresh nonce, so identity is the ledger. Forking an agent into parallel copies forces each branch to extend from the same last nonce, exposing identical ancestry and splitting accrued reputation. An attacker must sacrifice reputation per branch or redo all past work per copy at full compute cost, making fakes uneconomical — like rings in a cedar, currents at an inlet, roots of a juniper.
